summary: A limestone island 13 miles off Alpena, where the first tower fell down and a light has marked the Lake Huron shipping lane since 1832.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on: sequence of the first tower's fall (Lighthouse Friends: before completion; Pepper: after the first keeper); first keeper (Duchene vs Israel Noble); appropriation year (1830 Preservation Society, 1831 Lighthouse Friends); 1913 candlepower; 1921 vs 1923 diaphone; 1980 vs 1983 automation; fog building 1871/1892/1893/1906. The Light-House Board report volume labelled 1891 gives the Sept 20 working party in its fiscal-1891 section, so the year is 1890; Pepper says 1891. USLHS roster has no head keeper 1882-1894, but the Alpena Weekly Argus names Captain Sinclair 1887-1891. Page numbers for the Light-House Board reports are scan pages or omitted because OCR page data is unconfirmed; fog-signal hours were matched to fiscal years by the nearest running head. The Bulletin 1915 fog-hour table was OCR-scrambled and not used. The earlier reports (before 1891) are not in the corpus; their content comes via Pepper. Peter Romes's Preservation Society blog post (2024) was seen only as a headline. The island's life-saving station is a separate station not in the records; its keeper John D. Persons is linked to the assistant of the same name through the Preservation Society's history. The tower Nov 1913 storm and Coast Guardsman's 1963 account come from the Preservation Society site. Lens and light characteristic (record says Fl G 10s) not sourced, so omitted. Not read: the NRHP nomination (not digitised), Tongue's book Lanterns and Lifeboats, Lighthouse Digest. Fact-check 2026-10-27: Sinclair line now uses Lighthouse Friends' John Sinclair, Jr. (1882-1894) with the Argus mentions; 'from 1884' in the earlier draft had no source. Fog-signal hours were checked against the running heads of the Board volumes (1892, 1894, 1895, 1896, 1897 sections confirmed). Bulletin index numbers (29, 162) are page numbers within the 1924-29 volume, so the flag year is only 'between 1924 and 1929'.
